title_guess: Stagflation: when GDP falls while inflation rises

segments.teaches: the economy turns available resources (raw material, technology, capital, labour) into output (GDP); labour links to the unemployment rate

elements.what: Available Resources -> yellow ECONOMY box -> GDP Output
square-bullet resource list in blue
yellow outline around Labour
green up-arrow beside GDP
curved arrow from Labour to '% of unemployed workers'

segments.notes: Same economy block as E02 (natural rate); a shared template.

segments.teaches: growing GDP means firms produce more and hire more; unemployment falls, labour gets scarce and wages rise

elements.what: right column: growing GDP -> firms produce more (phrase highlighted green) -> hire more workers
left column: green box 'unemployed share starts decreasing' -> UNEMPLOYMENT with green down-arrow -> wage explanation
green highlight on a key phrase
green down-arrow beside UNEMPLOYMENT

segments.notes: Two parallel cause chains hang from the same flow diagram.

segments.teaches: higher labour cost is passed on to consumers as higher prices

elements.what: right chain extended in red: [higher labour cost] -> firms pass costs to consumers

segments.notes: Colour shift green -> red marks the turn from good news to inflation.

segments.teaches: normal pattern: GDP up means inflation up and unemployment down, and the reverse

elements.what: three light-blue columns GDP / INFLATION / UNEMPLOYMENT; cells increase/increase/decrease and decrease/decrease/increase pop in one at a time

segments.notes: This 3-column direction table is the video's home-base composition.

segments.teaches: the inflation-unemployment pair is the Phillips curve relationship

elements.what: thick black frame around the inflation and unemployment columns
big black chevron arrow to the right
grey card titled PHILLIPS CURVE: inflation vs unemployment curve with a red dot on the inflation axis and a yellow dot on the unemployment axis

segments.notes: Cross-reference to the Phillips curve video (E02) as a small inset card.

segments.teaches: GDP and inflation normally move together; the word stagflation joins 'stagnant growth' and 'inflation'

elements.what: black frame moves to the GDP and inflation columns; both rows get green bands
word split in two colours: FLATION with an up-arrow to Inflation, STAG with a down-arrow to stagnant growth
short up and down arrows from the word halves

segments.notes: Etymology trick: split the term into its two halves and point each half at its meaning.

segments.teaches: stagflation breaks the pattern: growth stagnates while inflation rises

elements.what: red STAGFLATION label to the left of a new row
new red-tinted row under the green rows: stagnant | increase
big black ? after the inflation cell

segments.notes: Anomaly row in red under two normal green rows, with a ? to open the 'how?' question.

segments.teaches: 1970s oil price shock: raw material costs jump, production costs and prices rise, demand falls and growth slows, so GDP falls while inflation rises

elements.what: red STAGFLATION chip at top right
economy block restored (resources -> ECONOMY -> GDP output)
light-blue box: oil price rise in the 1970s
oil barrel with dollar sign and rising chart
pink COST INCREASE band over Raw Material
red chain down the left: cost explanation -> INFLATION up -> reduced demand -> growth slows
red up-arrow beside INFLATION
red DECREASE under GDP output

segments.notes: Historical case worked through on the earlier economy diagram; chain runs down then right.

segments.teaches: summary: in stagflation GDP decreases and inflation increases

elements.what: direction table restored; red stagflation row now reads decrease | increase
red STAGFLATION label

segments.notes: Home-base table returns; the earlier 'stagnant ... ?' cells are replaced by the answer.
